By age five, he had his first professional engagement playing boogie-woogie piano, and at age ten received his first drum set from Dragnet actor Jack Webb.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Early immersion and access to professional mentors can dramatically accelerate musical mastery.

idea_cards.title: Swapping Licks with Hendrix
idea_cards.insight: In the late 1960s, Kowalski moved to London to form the blues-rock band The New Nadir. While performing regularly on the club circuit alongside legendary acts, Jimi Hendrix even dropped by to sit in and jam with the band.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Proximity to cultural epicenters opens doors to once-in-a-lifetime collaborative opportunities.

idea_cards.title: Backing the Beach Boys
idea_cards.insight: Following auditions in 1968, Kowalski became an integral touring and session percussionist and drummer for the Beach Boys. He filled in for Dennis Wilson during key historical moments and maintained a continuous touring presence with the band for over two decades.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Reliability and versatility turn short-term session gigs into decades-long career partnerships.

quiz.question: Which iconic rock guitarist once sat in to jam with Mike Kowalski's band, The New Nadir, in London?
quiz.explanation: While performing at the Speakeasy in London, a friend of guitarist Ed Carter sat in with The New Nadir, and that friend was Jimi Hendrix.

hook: Though criticized at first for being too frivolous for a serious national symbol, the charming Swiss 'Vreneli' gold coin became one of the most beloved and widely recognized bullion pieces in history.

idea_cards.title: The Origin of Vreneli
idea_cards.insight: The iconic design of the Swiss gold coin was created by Neuchâtel medalist Fritz Ulysse Landry. Initially criticized as too young and romantic with an intrusive alpine background, the design was revised to show a female head with a garland of edelweiss, eventually earning the affectionate diminutive nickname 'Vreneli'.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Public affection can easily override formal institutional critiques when art successfully captures cultural identity.

idea_cards.title: Denominations and Specifications
idea_cards.insight: Vreneli coins were minted in 10, 20, and 100 franc denominations to the strict standards of the Latin Monetary Union, containing 900-purity gold. While the 20 franc coin was mass-produced with tens of millions struck, the 100 franc version was minted exclusively in 1925 with a tiny run of just 5,000 pieces.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Rarity and historical production volume dictate modern numismatic value far beyond face value.

idea_cards.title: The Mystery of 1935 Restrikes
idea_cards.insight: Legal tender status for regular Vrenelis officially ceased in 1936, but massive market demand led the Swiss Mint to officially restrike millions of 20 franc coins dated 1935 marked with an 'L' for bullion. This means many coins dated 1935 were actually manufactured a decade later during the mid-to-late 1940s.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Always look beneath the surface date, as official institutional restrikes can alter the true chronology of physical assets.

quiz.question: What is the origin of the name 'Vreneli' given to these Swiss gold coins?
options: It is named after the Swiss canton where they were first discovered.
It is a Swiss German affectionate diminutive of the female given name Verena.
It is the ancient Latin word for financial prosperity.
quiz.explanation: The name Vreneli derives from a Swiss German affectionate diminutive of the female given name Verena, personifying the female youth and national symbol depicted on the coin.

hook: Born out of a patent lawsuit and a strategic acquisition, a small radio parts business transformed into the legendary wartime backbone of Allied communications.

idea_cards.title: A Name Born From Craft
idea_cards.insight: Founded in 1932 by William J. Halligan, the company name was a clever combination of his surname and the concept of handcrafted amateur radios. Early on, facing severe patent lawsuits from RCA, Halligan cleverly acquired another struggling company primarily just to secure their vital RCA patent license.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Leverage Assets. Overcome initial industry barriers by acquiring existing companies for their critical intellectual property rather than fighting from scratch.

idea_cards.title: The Wartime Defense Umbrella
idea_cards.insight: During World War II, Hallicrafters completely shifted its production from consumer ham radio gear to critical military hardware. Their mobile HF stations, such as the SCR-299 communications package, provided indispensable communication links for U.S. troops on the front lines.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Agility in Crisis. Survival and extreme growth often require temporarily abandoning consumer markets to fulfill urgent, high-stakes societal needs.

idea_cards.title: Industrial Design Meets Radio
idea_cards.insight: In the post-war boom years, Hallicrafters combined advanced engineering with stunning exterior design, collaborating with famous industrial designer Raymond Loewy on iconic models like the S-38 and SX-42. These radios transcended functional tools to become stylish household electronics.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Form Elevates Function. Merging cutting-edge technical performance with striking aesthetic design creates products that resonate deeply with consumers and collectors alike.

idea_cards.title: From Consumer Tech to Missiles
idea_cards.insight: As the Cold War escalated, Hallicrafters heavily participated in defense research, developing electronic warfare capabilities, missile ground support equipment, and penetration aids for ICBMs. Eventually, increased domestic market pressure from Japanese electronics and military shifts led to the end of non-military production in 1975.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Market Pivot and Competition. When low-cost international competition threatens domestic consumer lines, shifting deep technical R&D toward defense can extend a company's enterprise lifecycle.

quiz.question: What was the primary asset Hallicrafters gained by acquiring Silver-Marshall Inc. in 1933?
quiz.explanation: Hallicrafters faced severe patent difficulties with RCA when they first started. Acquiring Silver-Marshall Inc. provided them with a vital RCA patent license as its most valuable asset.

hook: Despite their iconic status in western expansion, the famous heavy Conestoga wagons were actually too massive to cross the Mississippi River and rarely made the westward trek.

idea_cards.title: The Heavy Conestoga Myth
idea_cards.insight: The iconic Conestoga wagon was a massive, boat-shaped freight vehicle capable of carrying up to five tons. Built in eastern North America without springs and supported by angled bows, it was simply too heavy for the grueling 2,000-mile trails west of the Mississippi.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Popular culture often blends distinct historical tools, misattributing eastern freight work to western migration.

idea_cards.title: Birth of Prairie Schooners
idea_cards.insight: As settlers headed west in the 1840s, they relied on lighter farm wagons fitted with white canvas tops. The nickname 'prairie schooner' was born because their billowing white covers resembled ship sails crossing an endless sea of grass.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Adaptability over strength—lighter, simpler tools often succeed where heavy, specialized machinery fails.

idea_cards.title: Oxen Over Horses
idea_cards.insight: While horses and mules were used, pioneer guidebooks strongly recommended oxen for pulling covered wagons. Oxen proved to be significantly more reliable, cheaper to maintain, and nearly as fast as their equine counterparts over long distances.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Prioritize endurance and reliability over raw speed when facing long-term, high-uncertainty endeavors.

idea_cards.title: Global Wagon Migrations
idea_cards.insight: Covered wagons were not unique to North America; Dutch-speaking settlers in South Africa used specialized trek wagons during the Great Trek of 1836. These long-wheelbase vehicles featured higher rear sides and served as mobile homes across unfamiliar terrain.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Universal challenges produce convergent architectural solutions across completely different continents and cultures.

quiz.question: Why were Conestoga wagons rarely used for westward migration across the United States?
options: They were too heavy for the long western trails
They were strictly reserved for military use
They were incapable of carrying canvas covers
quiz.explanation: Conestoga wagons weighed up to 5 tons and lacked springs, making them far too heavy for the rugged 2,000-mile journey west of the Mississippi River.

hook: A luxury cruise liner dubbed the 'Queen of the Lakes' turned into a fatal inferno in a matter of minutes due to a locked linen closet and lemon-oil-polished walls.

idea_cards.title: The Queen of the Lakes
idea_cards.insight: Launched in 1913, the SS Noronic was one of Canada's largest and most luxurious passenger ships, accommodating up to 600 passengers and 200 crew members across five grand decks. However, its upper passenger decks lacked direct gangplank access to the dock, concentrating all exits on the lowest deck.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Bottleneck Architecture. Always evaluate systems for single points of failure that restrict emergency egress.

idea_cards.title: Fatal Delay in Alarms
idea_cards.insight: When smoke was first spotted in a linen closet at 2:30 a.m., staff opted to fetch keys rather than immediately sounding the alarm or evacuating nearby cabins. By the time the ship's whistle finally blew eight minutes later, half of the vessel was already ablaze.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Prioritize immediate warning over investigation when facing potential high-consequence emergencies.

idea_cards.title: Combustible Luxury Materials
idea_cards.insight: The fire spread with terrifying speed because the interior walls were lined with wood paneling polished with flammable lemon oil. Combined with out-of-order fire extinguishers, the ship transformed into an inescapable trap for sleeping passengers.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Compound Risk. Aesthetic choices can inadvertently multiply catastrophic safety vulnerabilities.

quiz.question: What primary structural design flaw severely hampered the evacuation of passengers on the SS Noronic?
options: There were no lifeboats on board
All exits were restricted to the lowest deck
The ship had no stairs at all
quiz.explanation: None of the upper passenger decks had direct gangplank access, meaning all exits had to go through the lowest E deck, which quickly became blocked by fire.

hook: Twice a winner of the deadly 24 Hours of Le Mans, British racing driver Ivor Bueb earned motorsport immortality before a tragic crash ended an era.

idea_cards.title: From War to Racetracks
idea_cards.insight: Before becoming a legendary racing driver, Ivor Bueb served in the RAF during World War II and even earned his Aviator's Certificate piloting a Tiger Moth. He transitioned into motorsport in the early 1950s, quickly proving his natural talent in Formula Three and sports car racing.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Diverse early life experiences often build the resilience and adaptability needed for elite performance.

idea_cards.title: Conquering Le Mans Twice
idea_cards.insight: Bueb achieved his greatest fame by winning the grueling 24 Hours of Le Mans twice, first in 1955 alongside Mike Hawthorn in a Jaguar D-type, and again in 1957 with Ron Flockhart. The 1955 victory came during one of the darkest races in motorsport history, which was marred by a catastrophic spectator accident.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Peak achievement often requires maintaining composure and executing under extreme psychological pressure.

idea_cards.title: A Fatal Turning Point
idea_cards.insight: In 1959, Bueb suffered fatal injuries after crashing his Formula Two car at the treacherous Charade Circuit in France. His tragic death, following the loss of fellow driver Archie Scott Brown, directly prompted constructor Brian Lister to shut down his legendary sports car racing operation.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: High-risk environments frequently undergo structural changes only after compounding tragedies force safety reform.

quiz.question: Which prestigious endurance race did Ivor Bueb win twice during his career?
quiz.explanation: Ivor Bueb won the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1955 alongside Mike Hawthorn and again in 1957 with Ron Flockhart.

hook: Eminem's blistering political protest song built up to look like an impending violent revolution ultimately redirected its angry mob straight to the ballot box.

idea_cards.title: Strategic Pre-Election Timing
idea_cards.insight: Released just one week before the 2004 presidential election, 'Mosh' was designed as a direct protest against George W. Bush and his administration's war policies. Although dropped too late to impact most voter registration deadlines, it seized maximum cultural visibility right when political tensions peaked.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Urgency matters, but structural deadlines dictate whether timely art can alter real-world logistics.

idea_cards.title: The Subversive Animated Video
idea_cards.insight: Directed by Ian Inaba, the music video portrays Eminem rallying a uniform army of hoodies marching angrily toward the White House. Rather than initiating a violent overthrow, the cinematic tension resolves peacefully as the crowd simply signs up to vote.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Subversion through misdirection—harnessing the aesthetic of rebellion to champion civic duty.

idea_cards.title: Targeting Real Power
idea_cards.insight: Critics noted that the track represented a rare moment where Eminem shifted his focus from low-hanging scapegoats to figures holding actual systemic power. Backed by Dr. Dre's apocalyptic production, his righteous anger found a tangible target in the Commander-in-Chief.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Punch up, not down; true impact comes from confronting the architects of systemic issues.

quiz.question: What is the surprising twist at the climax of the music video for Eminem's 'Mosh'?
options: The crowd storms the White House and physically deposes the president
The angry mob peacefully registers and signs up to vote
Eminem tears up an American flag in front of live cameras
quiz.explanation: Despite appearing to lead a violent rebellion dressed in dark hoodies, Eminem's followers' ultimate charge is directed straight to the voting booth.

hook: Imagine surviving heavy depth charges and enemy bombs, only to be accidentally fired upon by your own allies in the open ocean.

idea_cards.title: A Daring Surface Attack
idea_cards.insight: During her third war patrol, the USS Bream targeted an Imperial Japanese Navy heavy cruiser, the Aoba, closing in to launch a deadly spread of torpedoes. Although she did not sink the vessel, the severe damage inflicted by Bream successfully kept the heavy cruiser out of the pivotal Battle of Leyte Gulf.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Bold calculated risks can yield disproportionately massive strategic impacts even without complete destruction.

idea_cards.title: Friendly Fire in the Coral Sea
idea_cards.insight: While en route to her combat zones in the Pacific, an Allied Liberty ship mistook the Bream for an enemy submarine and opened fire with multiple rounds. Fortunately, the submarine suffered no casualties or damage, highlighting the perilous confusion of wartime coordination.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Fog of War — recognize that in complex environments, allies and systems can pose unexpected risks.

idea_cards.title: Enduring War Patrols
idea_cards.insight: The Gato-class submarine completed six demanding war patrols across perilous Southeast Asian waters, sinking enemy ships and weathering intense depth-charging. Despite flooding incidents, mechanical fires, and aerial bomb attacks, the ship repeatedly bounced back after refits.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: True resilience is the ability to absorb systemic shocks, repair the damage, and stay operational.

quiz.question: Which Japanese warship did the USS Bream severely damage during her third war patrol, preventing it from participating in the Battle of Leyte Gulf?
quiz.explanation: On 23 October 1944, the USS Bream attacked a Japanese naval force and severely damaged the heavy cruiser Aoba.

hook: Imagine serving at the highest levels of national government, holding powerful portfolios like Defence and Justice, and later turning down a seat to return to Parliament.

idea_cards.title: From Immigrant to Cabinet Minister
idea_cards.insight: Born in England, Mark Burton moved to New Zealand at age ten and built a strong foundation in community service. His extensive work with social organizations earned him the New Zealand 1990 Commemoration Medal before he entered national politics.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Deep community involvement serves as a powerful springboard for public service leadership.

idea_cards.title: Handling High-Stakes Portfolios
idea_cards.insight: When the Labour Party won power in 1999, Burton stepped into demanding cabinet roles, eventually managing Defence, Justice, and Treaty of Waitangi Negotiations. He navigated complex government responsibilities during a pivotal era for New Zealand.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Versatility allows leaders to effectively steward diverse and high-pressure domains.

idea_cards.title: Shaping Electoral Transparency
idea_cards.insight: As a key legislator, Burton sponsored the Electoral Finance Act to regulate political contributions and curb anonymous donations. This initiative fundamentally aimed to make campaign funding more open and accessible to a broader range of parties.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Institutional reforms often focus on transparency to restore and maintain public trust.

quiz.question: Which major cabinet portfolio did Mark Burton hold during the Fifth Labour Government of New Zealand?
quiz.explanation: Mark Burton served in several prominent cabinet roles, including Minister of Defence, Minister of Justice, and Minister of Local Government.

hook: Despite sounding entirely distinct today, Hungarian shares a deeply rooted linguistic branch with two Siberian languages, Khanty and Mansi, bound by ancient horse motifs and shared vocabulary.

idea_cards.title: The Three Ugric Branches
idea_cards.insight: The Ugric branch of the Uralic language family consists of Hungarian, Khanty, and Mansi. While Hungarian is spoken in Central Europe, Khanty and Mansi are spoken in Siberia, yet they still retain critical ancestral linguistic ties.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Geographic distance does not erase deep genetic linguistic roots.

idea_cards.title: Shared Steppe Vocabulary
idea_cards.insight: Ugric languages share specialized terminology not found elsewhere in the Uralic family, most notably words for 'horse' and 'saddle'. This suggests Proto-Ugric speakers lived in close contact with nomadic steppe communities in southern Siberia.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Shared specialized vocabulary reveals ancestral lifestyles and environments.

idea_cards.title: Phonetic and Structural Clues
idea_cards.insight: Linguists trace connections using unique anomalies, such as the numeral '3', which points to an original consonant cluster in both Hungarian and Mansi. They also share structural traits like distinct verb conjugations based on object definiteness.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Irregularities and shared anomalies are often the strongest clues to common ancestry.

quiz.question: Which three languages make up the Ugric branch of the Uralic language family?
quiz.explanation: Ugric includes three primary subgroups: Hungarian, Khanty, and Mansi, with the latter two often grouped together as Ob-Ugric.

hook: Did you know that one of Chicago's only three minor basilicas started its life as a relocated portable wood-frame building?

idea_cards.title: Humble Beginnings in Chicago
idea_cards.insight: Established in 1929 after petitioning Cardinal George Mundelein, the parish initially used a relocated portable wood-frame church from Oak Park. The surrounding neighborhood quickly grew after World War II, attracting many Irish and German immigrant families.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Incremental Growth. Big institutions often start as small, temporary structures before scaling into permanent architectural icons.

idea_cards.title: Design and Papal Elevation
idea_cards.insight: Designed in a stunning Neo-Gothic style by architects Meyer and Cook, the permanent structure was finally completed in 1960. Recognizing its architectural and spiritual significance, Pope John XXIII elevated the church to a minor basilica in 1962.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Lasting impact is built through patience, deliberate design, and eventual recognition of excellence.

idea_cards.title: Universal Shrines in Glass
idea_cards.insight: The massive window over the choir loft brilliantly features eight distinct shrines of the Virgin Mary from around the world. This artistic choice deliberately bridges cultural barriers, uniting diverse ethnic groups under a single shared spiritual theme.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Cultural Synthesis. Shared core values can effectively bridge and unite diverse demographic backgrounds.

quiz.question: What kind of structure was initially used as the first church building for the parish in 1929?
options: A portable wood-frame church relocated from Oak Park
A stone chapel built by early settlers
quiz.explanation: The initial church structure was a portable wood-frame church that previously served as St. Giles Church in nearby Oak Park.

hook: Despite its distinct almond flavor, traditional Italian amaretto is often crafted without nuts at all, drawing its signature taste instead from steeped apricot kernels and peach stones.

idea_cards.title: Almond Taste Without Actual Almonds
idea_cards.insight: Amaretto gets its signature nutty flavor primarily from benzaldehyde, a natural compound abundant in fruit pits like apricot kernels and peach stones. While some recipes use bitter almonds, many major producers rely entirely on stone fruit seeds steeped in alcohol to produce its iconic aroma.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Chemical Equivalency — Strikingly similar flavors can be derived from surprising, non-intuitive natural sources sharing common aromatic compounds.

idea_cards.title: A Renaissance Gift of Love
idea_cards.insight: Legend traces amaretto to 1525, when painter Bernardino Luini, a pupil of Leonardo da Vinci, used a young widowed innkeeper in Saronno as his model for a church fresco. Lacking monetary wealth to show her gratitude, she steeped apricot kernels in brandy, inventing the sweet liqueur as a romantic gift.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Resourceful Creation — World-famous culinary traditions often emerge from simple ingredients paired with human creativity and affection.

idea_cards.title: Amaretto Is Not Amaro
idea_cards.insight: Although 'amaretto' translates to 'a little bitter', its bitterness is mild and tempered by added sweetening agents. It remains entirely distinct from Italian 'amaro', a vastly different category of bitter liqueurs distilled from medicinal herbs, roots, barks, and citrus peels.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Label Precision — Near-identical linguistic roots can mask completely different products, making context crucial in culinary terminology.

quiz.question: What organic compound provides amaretto with its signature almond-like flavor?
quiz.explanation: Benzaldehyde naturally occurs in apricot kernels, peach stones, and almonds, giving amaretto its distinctive nutty scent and flavor.

hook: Emperor Charles VI spent a decade bribing and trading European territories just to ensure his unborn daughters could inherit a throne that Salic law said belonged to men.

idea_cards.title: A Desperate Imperial Obsession
idea_cards.insight: With the male Habsburg line dying out, Emperor Charles VI faced a massive constitutional crisis because traditional Salic law prohibited female inheritance. He issued the Pragmatic Sanction in 1713 to guarantee that his future, yet-unborn daughters could inherit the vast Habsburg lands undivided. Securing this legal change became his absolute life obsession, altering prior pacts that favored his older brother's daughters.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Anticipating structural failures allows leaders to redesign rules before a crisis strikes.

idea_cards.title: Trading Land For Recognition
idea_cards.insight: Because other European powers were eager to contest a female succession, Charles VI spent ten grueling years buying international recognition. He made heavy concessions, such as sacrificing overseas trading companies, ceding territory, and giving up Italian lands to get major courts to sign off on the edict. Despite all his diplomatic maneuvering, the moment he died, the agreement was immediately challenged.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Paper agreements without aligned incentives or raw power often collapse under pressure.

idea_cards.title: The War Of Succession
idea_cards.insight: True to fears, Charles's daughter Maria Theresa faced an immediate military onslaught upon taking the throne in 1740, triggering the War of the Austrian Succession. Backed by rivals like France and Bavaria, enemies sought to carve up the Habsburg empire despite the Sanction. Maria Theresa successfully defended her crown, proving that survival ultimately relied on military resilience rather than legal documents alone.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Legality provides a framework, but execution and defense preserve your assets.

quiz.question: What primary legal restriction forced Emperor Charles VI to issue the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713?
options: Salic law prohibited female inheritance of the Habsburg lands
The Pope refused to crown any monarch without a written edict
The Hungarian parliament banned foreign rulers permanently
quiz.explanation: Salic law forbade women from inheriting the throne, which meant Charles VI had to create the Pragmatic Sanction to allow his daughters to succeed him.

hook: Built directly on one of the most volatile volcanic zones on Earth, Leilani Estates discovered overnight that nature always reclaims what is hers.

idea_cards.title: Living on Active Volcanic Zones
idea_cards.insight: Leilani Estates is situated directly on the lower East Rift Zone of Kīlauea volcano, categorized within lava flow hazard zone 1. This means new eruptive vents can and do spawn anywhere within the subdivision, putting homes directly in nature's path.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Mental Model: Hazard Zones Demand Ultimate Respect for Geological Realities.

idea_cards.title: The Devastating 2018 Eruption
idea_cards.insight: During the 2018 Kīlauea eruption, 14 out of 24 total volcanic fissure vents opened directly inside the Leilani Estates subdivision. The dominant vent, ʻAhuʻailāʻau, unleashed fountains up to 330 feet high and destroyed around 200 homes.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Cataclysmic natural events can completely reshape a community in a matter of days.

idea_cards.title: Protecting Privacy After Disaster
idea_cards.insight: Following the eruption, local authorities and the Leilani Community Association strictly prohibited access to the solid lava rock flow field. Fines up to $5,000 and strict anti-trespassing regulations were enforced to prevent the disaster zone from becoming a morbid public tourist attraction.
idea_cards.key_takeaway: Takeaway: Communities deserve dignity and privacy during recovery, shielding tragedies from voyeurism.

quiz.question: Which dominant volcanic fissure vent produced the most lava and fountained up to 330 feet high in Leilani Estates during 2018?
